product.title: 32% ‘fully trust' their AI agents. 4 in 10 of them still approve every action
product.summary: Nylas surveyed 1,030 AI builders and buyers. 32% said they fully trust an agent to run on its own, yet 4 in 10 of them require human approval on every action. Trust depends on the task: teams will let an agent schedule a meeting (56%) long before they'll let it email a customer (44%) or change a system setting (27%). product.title: Why Do the Business Case If Nobody Asks You To?
product.summary: Product managers can apply everyday business thinking and customer discovery during delivery planning even without a formal business case. By examining customer needs, projects, and operational costs, teams align delivery with real business opportunities and resolve open decisions through lightweight insights.

product.title: Good Product Development Teams Have Messy Boundaries
product.summary: High-performing product teams thrive on flexible boundaries rather than rigid sequential handoffs. By aligning on shared milestones and maintaining cross-functional trust, teams navigate different timeline requirements across hardware and software to build complex products more effectively.

product.title: The Data Driven Illusion
product.summary: Most organizations operate under a data-driven illusion, using data to confirm existing opinions rather than discover real insights. True data-driven cultures prioritize uncovering raw insights before setting goals, which requires structural shifts toward insight-first pitching.

tech.title: SpaceX and Tesla Talks on Record Merger Are Said to Progress
tech.summary: SpaceX and Tesla could announce a merger deal as soon as December. The companies' boards and advisers are working out the terms of the deal and the governance structure of the combined entity. The merger will be a major test case for political sentiment following the US midterm elections. The aggressive timeline reflects Elon Musk's tendency to move quickly when it comes to corporate maneuvers.

tech.title: Jensen Huang Has Been Ousted as Nvidia CEO
tech.summary: Jensen Huang has resigned as Nvidia's CEO after the revelation of two extramarital affairs. Finance chief Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO until a permanent successor is named. The board is considering both internal and external candidates. Nvidia's board has appointed long-time director Harvey C. Jones as its first ever chair. Huang has previously said that he doesn't believe in succession planning and that leaders should continuously pass on knowledge and information as they have it.

tech.title: A DeepSeek Moment for Biotech
tech.summary: Chinese drugmakers account for at least a third of the world's pipeline of innovative drugs in development, but China-originated novel treatments have yet to reach overseas markets at scale. The country runs more clinical trials than any place else. Chinese drugmakers with global ambitions currently pursue them primarily through partnerships with Western companies, who usually take charge of late-stage development and eventual sales of the drugs outside of China. Some lawmakers in the US are calling for restrictions on partnerships with Chinese companies, but industry analysts say the business momentum is too strong to break.

tech.title: The Next Chapter of mRNA
tech.summary: mRNA technology has the potential to generate hundreds of new treatments for a range of diseases. It is quickly becoming the preferred technology for its speed - a vaccine can be created against any pathogen within six to eight weeks, less time than it takes to conduct the studies required to establish a therapy's safety and efficacy. The technology could redesign treatments in infectious diseases, rare diseases, and cancer.

tech.title: 4 in 10 leaders say humanoid robots will never be viable for mass deployment
tech.summary: Intel asked 800 senior business, IT and robotics leaders which robots will matter most in their industry over the next five years. Humanoids got 6% of the votes . 77% said reliability matters more than what a robot looks like. See the full breakdown in Intel's Robotics Readiness Gap report.

tech.title: Slop Is Moving Up the Stack
tech.summary: AI is writing significantly less slop, but slop has not been eliminated. Slop has now moved up the stack to infest design decisions. Frontier agents lack foresight into how their code will be used. They display poor abstraction design and complete disregard for reusing library-provided code.

tech.title: Bad ideas that aren't bad anymore
tech.summary: You develop a lot of intuition throughout your career through experience. This knowledge and experience is what makes leaders effective. However, once in a while, it's worth revisiting ideas that were once considered bad. Some of the intuition you're relying on might not be worth as much anymore, as things change.

tech.title: AI Company Employees Should Unionize
tech.summary: Safety-conscious employees at AI companies should unionize, as this would give them the power to keep their employers in check if they have concerns about their work. There are so few skilled AI researchers that companies will want to negotiate if a dozen top AI researchers threaten to walk. A union would uphold normal protections around discipline and firing, demand transparency, and act as an independent voice to hold companies to their commitments. RSI could make AI employees obsolete as soon as next year, so they need to take action now, as they may never have this amount of leverage again.

tech.title: Google pushes privacy angle as Gemini-powered smartglasses debut starting at $395
tech.summary: Google has partnered with Samsung, Gentle Monster, and Warby Parker to create Gemini-powered smartglasses. The frames, which all weigh around 41 grams, will have a camera that Gemini can use for tasks. The assistant will have access to user data and preferences to produce personalized answers. Google claims it has implemented a number of features and limitations to ensure that people don't do creepy things with the device, and that it doesn't do creepy things to users.
